sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ devayanto havante sarasvatīm adhvare tāyamāne | sarasvatīṃ sukṛto hvayanta sarasvatī dāśuṣe vāryaṃ dāt ||
english: Those who seek the gods call upon Sarasvatī; they call upon Sarasvatī when the sacrifice is spread. The pious call upon Sarasvatī; may Sarasvatī grant the choicest boon to the worshipper.

sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ yāṃ pitaro havante dakṣiṇā yajñam abhinakṣamāṇāḥ | āsadyāsmin barhiṣi mādayasva- -anamīvā iṣa ā dhehy asme ||
english: That Sarasvatī whom the Fathers invoke while they approach the sacrifice from the south — be seated on this sacred grass and rejoice; place within us food that is free from disease.

sanskrit: sarasvatī yā sarathaṃ yayātha- -ukthaiḥ svadhābhir devi pitṛbhir madantī | sahasrārgham iḍo atra bhāgaṃ rāyaspoṣaṃ yajamānāya dhehi ||
english: O Sarasvatī, who hast ridden on the same chariot with the Fathers, rejoicing, O goddess, with the praises and the ancestral offerings — bestow here the portion of refreshment worth a thousand, and grant abundance of wealth to the sacrificer.

sanskrit: ud īratām avara ut parāsa un madhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ | asuṃ ya īyur avṛkā ṛtajñās te no 'vantu pitaro haveṣu ||
english: Let the lower Fathers rise up, let the higher ones rise up, let the middle Fathers, who belong to Soma, rise up. They who have gone to the realm of breath, free from harm, knowing the sacred order — may those Fathers aid us at our invocations.

sanskrit: āhaṃ pitṝn suvidatrām̐ avitsi napātaṃ ca vikramaṇaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ | barhiṣado ye svadhayā sutasya bhajanta pitvas ta ihāgamiṣṭhāḥ ||
english: I have found the Fathers who grant good gifts, and also the grandson and the wide stride of Viṣṇu. Those who sit upon the sacred grass and share in the pressed drink with the ancestral oblation — may they come here most readily.

sanskrit: idaṃ pitṛbhya ity ekā ||
english: "This to the Fathers" — so one verse.

sanskrit: mātalī kavair yamo aṅgirobhir bṛhaspatir ṛkmabhir vāvṛdhānaḥ | yāṃś ca devā vāvṛdhur ye ca devān svāhān ye svadhayān ye madanti ||
english: Mātali is magnified among the wise ones, Yama among the Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati among those rich in hymns. Both those whom the gods have magnified and those who have magnified the gods — those who rejoice in svāhā and those who rejoice in svadhā.

sanskrit: svāduṣ kilāyaṃ madhumām̐ utāyaṃ tīvraḥ kilāyaṃ rasavām̐ utāyam | uto nv asya papivām̐sam indraṃ na kaś cana sahata āhaveṣu ||
english: Sweet indeed is this drink, and full of honey; sharp indeed is this drink, and full of flavor. And now none among those who have drunk it can overcome Indra in battles.

sanskrit: pareyivāṃsaṃ pravato mahīr anu bahubhyaḥ panthām anupaspaśānaḥ | vaivasvataṃ saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ yamaṃ rājānaṃ haviṣā duvasya ||
english: Honor with oblation King Yama, son of Vivasvat, the gatherer of peoples — he who has crossed over the great descending slopes, surveying the path for the many.

sanskrit: yamo no gātuṃ prathamo viveda naiṣā gavyūtir apabhartavā u | yatrā naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ pareyur enā jajñānāḥ pathyā anu svāḥ ||
english: Yama first found the path for us; this pasture is not to be taken away. Where our ancient Fathers went forth — those born along it follow their own proper paths.

sanskrit: barhiṣadaḥ pitara ūty arvāg imā vo havyā cakṛmā juṣadhvam | ta ā gatāvasā śaṃtamena- -athā naḥ śaṃ yor arapo dadhāta ||
english: O Fathers who sit on the sacred grass, come hither to our aid; enjoy these oblations we have made for you. Come with the most beneficent help, and then bestow on us freedom from affliction and well-being.

sanskrit: ācyā jānu dakṣiṇato niṣadya- -imaṃ yajñam abhi gṛṇīta viśve | mā hiṃsiṣṭa pitaraḥ kena cin no yad va āgaḥ puruṣatā karāma ||
english: Having bent the knee and sat down to the south, all of you acclaim this sacrifice. Do not harm us, O Fathers, for any offense of a human nature that we have committed against you.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇoti- -idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sam eti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamāṇā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ prepares the wedding procession for his daughter; all this universe comes together. The mother of Yama, being led in the bridal procession, disappeared — the great wife of Vivasvat.

sanskrit: prehi prehi pathibhiḥ pūrvebhir yatrā te pūrve pitaraḥ paretāḥ | ubhā rājānā svadhayā madantā yamaṃ paśyāsi varuṇaṃ ca devam ||
english: Go forth, go forth by the ancient paths, to where your ancient Fathers have departed. You shall see the two kings, both rejoicing in the ancestral oblation — Yama and the god Varuṇa.

sanskrit: apeta vīta vi ca sarpatāto 'sma etaṃ pitaro lokam akran | ahobhir adbhir aktubhir vyaktaṃ yamo dadāty avasānam asmai ||
english: Depart, withdraw, and scatter from here — the Fathers have made this world for us. With days, with waters, and with nights, made distinct, Yama gives this one a resting place.

sanskrit: uśantas tvā ni dhīmahy uśantaḥ sam idhīmahi | uśann uśata ā vaha pitṝn haviṣe attave ||
english: Desiring thee, we lay thee down; desiring, we kindle thee. Do thou, willing, bring the willing Fathers to eat the oblation.

sanskrit: dyumantas tvā ni dhīmahi dyumantaḥ sam idhīmahi | dyumān dyumata ā vaha pitṝn haviṣe attave ||
english: Radiant, we lay thee down; radiant, we kindle thee. Do thou, shining, bring the shining Fathers to eat the oblation.

sanskrit: aṅgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāsaḥ | teṣāṃ vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyānām api bhadre saumanase syāma ||
english: The Aṅgiras are our Fathers, the Navagvas, the Atharvans, the Bhṛgus, who belong to Soma. May we be in the good grace and in the auspicious goodwill of those who are worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: aṅgirobhir yajñiyair ā gahīha yama vairūpair iha mādayasva | vivasvantaṃ huve yaḥ pitā te asmin yajñe barhiṣy ā niṣadya ||
english: Come here, O Yama, with the Aṅgiras worthy of sacrifice; rejoice here with the Vairūpas. I invoke Vivasvat, who is thy father — having sat down on the sacred grass at this sacrifice.

sanskrit: imaṃ yama prastaram ā hi sīda- -aṅgirobhiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ | ā tvā mantrāḥ kaviśastā vahanty enā rājan haviṣo mādayasva ||
english: Sit down upon this sacred strewn grass, O Yama, in agreement with the Aṅgiras Fathers. The hymns praised by the wise bring thee here — with these, O king, take delight in the oblation.

sanskrit: yamāya somaṃ sunuta yamāya juhutā haviḥ | yamaṃ ha yajño gacchatv agnidūto araṃkṛtaḥ ||
english: Press the Soma for Yama; pour the oblation for Yama. Let the sacrifice go to Yama, well-prepared, with Agni as its messenger.

sanskrit: yamāya ghṛtavad dhavir juhotā pra ca tiṣṭhata | sa no jīveṣv ā yamad dīrgham āyuṣ yad īyase ||
english: Pour the oblation rich in ghee for Yama and step forward. May he bind us among the living with long life as thou goest.

sanskrit: yamāya madhumattamaṃ rājñe havyaṃ juhotana | idaṃ nama ṛṣibhyaḥ pūrvajebhyaḥ pūrvebhyaḥ pathikṛdbhyaḥ ||
english: Pour for King Yama the most honey-sweet oblation. This homage is to the seers, the firstborn, the ancient ones, the path-makers.

sanskrit: trikadrukebhiḥ patati ṣaḍ urvīr ekam id bṛhat | triṣṭub gāyatrī chandāṃsi sarvā tā yama ārpitā ||
english: He flies by means of the three Kadrukas across the six broad spaces, that one great expanse. The Triṣṭubh, the Gāyatrī, the metres — all those are fixed in Yama.

sanskrit: mainam agne vi daho mā vi śoco māsya tvacaṃ cakṣuṣo mā śarīram | yadā śṛtaṃ kṛṇavo jātavedo 'them enaṃ pra hiṇutāt pitṛbhyaḥ ||
english: Do not burn him entirely, O Agni; do not scorch him; do not consume his skin, his eye, or his body. When thou hast matured him, O Jātavedas, then send him forth to the Fathers.

sanskrit: śṛtaṃ yadā karasi jātavedo 'them enaṃ pari dattāt pitṛbhyaḥ | yadā gacchāty asunītim eṣo 'thā devānāṃ vaśanīr bhavāti ||
english: When thou hast matured him, O Jātavedas, then hand him over to the Fathers all around. When this one goes to the guidance of the breath, then he shall become subject to the will of the gods.

sanskrit: sūryaṃ cakṣur gacchatu vātam ātmā divaṃ ca gaccha pṛthivīṃ ca dharmaṇā | apo vā gaccha yadi tatra te hitam oṣadhīṣu prati tiṣṭhā śarīraiḥ ||
english: Let the eye go to the sun, the breath to the wind; go to heaven and to the earth according to the sacred law. Or go to the waters, if that is thy destiny — take thy stand in the plants with thy bodily parts.
